failures.evidence: Red test TestADocumentSocketHoldsItsAwarenessBoundThroughARealUpgrade in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs/awareness_limit_upgrade_test.go (commit da4bb1a5). Command: cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<url> go test -run TestADocumentSocketHoldsItsAwarenessBoundThroughARealUpgrade ./internal/dispatch/docs. In workspace mode, which is how CI's envoy-go job and every local and browser-harness build run, it fails 2 of 2: 'carol on task A holds 10 of them, bob on task B 1; want at most 4 each'. With GOWORK=off it passes 2 of 2. Cause: the root go.work resolves github.com/gorilla/websocket v1.5.4-0.20250319132907-e064f32e3674 (packages/envoy/go.mod says v1.5.3). That version's Upgrade reads through the hijacked brw.Reader without resetting it onto the returned connection (server.go:192-195), so awarenessLimitConn.Read is never called. Temporary prints showed Hijack called for every socket and Read never. On two real binaries in workspace mode: one socket's 2,048-client frame reaches every reader on A and B; a 600-byte first message is not closed; 200 flooding sockets fill A's 4,000-client room, and a joining reader is seen by nobody within 1 s. The image build (Dockerfile, no go.work, gorilla v1.5.3) has the filter working. One possible fix: in awarenessLimitWriter.Hijack, reset buffers.Reader onto the filter connection, as keepAliveWriter.Hijack does for the writer.

observedWithTheFilterActive: GOWORK=off (gorilla v1.5.3, as the image builds), two real binaries. All three flood tests pass unmodified. 400,000 invented ids in 6 s: A 58 to 63 MB (live) and 54 to 62 MB (null), B unchanged. A live flood re-announced every 10 s from one socket: A 57 to 59 MB, B holds 4 of the socket's clients. From 200 sockets: B holds 92, and a joining reader is seen on both processes within 1 s.

Real browsers on main's two-process harness with a GOWORK=off harness binary (go version -m: gorilla v1.5.3): six tabs, three per process, place carets at once and each page shows the other five within 1 s, 4 rounds (also 3x under workspace mode); a tab on B whose socket is cut is shown on A again within 166-235 ms over 6 reconnects; coedit.multiprocess passes.

Census entry 4 through its own client: the web client's first message on each document socket is its Auth message (type 2), naming the document in a 38-byte header (41 bytes total), on A and B. A 600-byte name is closed; a well-formed awareness or sync message is kept. A 3-byte message naming nothing is passed to ygo and the socket stays open, which the census text ('a document socket whose first message names no document and type within 512 bytes is closed') does not say: text or code needs to change.
notes: Outside this round's scope, in the relay since round 1: ygo's relay lane keeps one awareness blob per room, latest only (internal/relaylane/lane.go:22-23, 111-115). Each blob encodes only the clients its change touched, so concurrent cursor changes from several sockets are lost until each client's next heartbeat (15 s for a browser). A Go probe with five readers on A setting cursors at once left bob on B missing some in 6 of 6 runs at 3b94b7c2 and 2 of 3 at d7ceabb4. Real browsers did not hit it in 15 rounds. Sent to the architect for a decision.
The repeated-flood test's text is unchanged, but its limit rose from 512 to 8,000 because maxAwarenessClientsPerRoom is now maxRoomConnections x 4.
